skill: Communicating between the technical and non-technical
expected_level_description: You can: - communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders - support and host discussions within a multidisciplinary team, with potentially difficult dynamics - be an advocate for the team externally - manage differing stakeholder perspectives
You can: - undertake data profiling and source system analysis - present clear insights to colleagues to support the end use of the data

You can: - develop a basic understanding of an unfamiliar or emerging technology, or a familiar technology in a new data context, with guidance - share what you learn with colleagues, including how it could help deliver more value from data

You can: - produce data models and understand where to use different types of data models - understand different tools and can compare different data models - reverse-engineer a data model from a live system - understand industry-recognised data modelling patterns and standards

You can: - use metadata repositories to complete complex tasks such as data and systems integration impact analysis - maintain a metadata repository to ensure information remains accurate and up to date

You can: - investigate problems in systems, processes and services, with an understanding of the level of a problem, for example, strategic, tactical or operational - contribute to the implementation of remedies and preventative measures

skill: Programming and build (data and analytics engineering)
expected_level_description: You can: - design, code, test and deploy programs or scripts following standards and good practice - write readable, maintainable code - use automation to improve the software development life cycle - consider and adopt appropriate security measures in your solutions
You can: - correctly execute test scripts under supervision - understand the role of testing and how it works

skill: Turning business problems into data design
expected_level_description: You can: - design data architecture by dealing with specific business problems and aligning it to enterprise-wide standards and principles - work within the context of well understood architecture, and identify appropriate patterns

You can: - explain the clinical and care workflows your work supports - use common health care terms correctly with clinical and care colleagues - recognise when a change could affect patient care and raise it
You can: - apply data protection principles to your work - contribute to data protection impact assessments - handle information requests and records correctly
You can: - run data quality checks and correct errors - explain data quality reports to colleagues
You can: - find and use the right codes for a data item or form - use terminology browsers and reference sets
You can: - explain the difference between identifiable, pseudonymised, and anonymised data - follow the organisation's rules for suppressing small numbers in outputs
